MAJOR: Baseline grandfathering file (`config/delivery-completeness-baseline.json`) has no stated monotonic-decrease enforcement, owner/expiry, or review gate; new placeholder completions can be added to it and silently defeat the gate.

RCCA-block trigger is keyword-based ("title/AC mentions RCCA"): brittle both ways — false positives on incidental mentions, evasions via paraphrase ("root cause analysis"). Prefer an explicit item type/label, or document the trigger precisely.

CI wiring is not fail-closed specified: acceptance requires `--report` (dry-run) support but does not state that `ci-cd-gates.json`/precheck invoke the enforcing (non-dry-run) mode with non-zero exit on error, crash, or unreadable backlog — a crash or misconfigured flag becomes a silent pass.

Design does not demonstrate the design-guardrail checklist (reversibility, invariants, observability, reuse) nor dispositions of prior Gate 1.5 findings (CL-006/CL-008); approval validity depends on this being embedded before Gate 1.5.
MINOR: Placeholder predicate ("specific" = not title echo, not `Objective achieved:`, length threshold) is heuristic and stated only in prose; the exact predicate, thresholds, and their tests are not pinned, risking drift between script and test-framework tests.
Baseline entries are implicitly keyed by item id; renames/deletions or id reuse can cause stale entries that mask or falsely fail items — no reconciliation step stated.
No observability statement for the gate (structured log line, counts of scanned/failed/baselined items, exit-reason) — checklist 10 diagnostics missing.
Precheck fast tier latency impact of full-backlog scan not bounded; consider caching or incremental scope.
NIT: Placeholder predicate logic likely duplicated across gate script and tests; extract a single predicate module for reuse.
Language rule is satisfied (tooling Python), but a one-line note in the design stating why this is tooling, not shipped runtime logic, would preempt a Gate 2 challenge.
SUMMARY: Sound direction: evidence-based DoD gate with dry-run, self-test, baseline audit, and CI wiring addresses the real closure-without-evidence failure mode.
Top risks: baseline can become a permanent escape hatch (no shrink-only/expiry rule), keyword-triggered RCCA validation is brittle, and CI fail-closed semantics are unspecified.
No blocker; proceed after tightening baseline governance, trigger definition, and fail-closed exit behavior.
